title: EGS Suzetrigine Study: A Randomized Controlled Trial
official: Preoperative Loading Versus Postoperative Initiation of Suzetrigine Versus Usual Care for Analgesia in Emergency General Surgery Patients: An Investigator-Initiated, Prospective, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether adding suzetrigine to usual pain treatment helps adults have better pain control after urgent or emergent general surgery. The study will also compare starting suzetrigine before surgery with starting it after surgery to see if one provides better pain relief.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does suzetrigine lower patient-reported pain after surgery?
* Does starting suzetrigine before surgery lower patient-reported pain significantly more than starting it after surgery?
* Does suzetrigine decrease patients' opioid use after surgery?

Researchers will compare the addition of suzetrigine to usual pain control treatment alone to see if suzetrigine helps reduce pain levels after surgery.

Participants will:

* Take suzetrigine every 12 hours for 14 days after the initial dose if assigned to Arms 1 or 2
* Report their pain levels at 6 hours, 24 hours, and 48 hours after surgery
* Report pain level, symptoms, and medication adherence over phone call at 14 days and 30 days after surgery
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥18 years.
* Requires urgent or emergent (non-elective) appendectomy or cholecystectomy operative intervention.
* Able to provide legally effective informed consent, as demonstrated by the ability to understand the purpose and procedures of the study, consider the implications of participation, communication a voluntary decision, and report pain using the 0-10 numeric rating scale.
* Able to swallow whole oral tablets, with preoperative administration considered clinically appropriate by the treating surgical and anesthesia teams.
* Sufficient anticipated time after consent and randomization to administer the preoperative loading dose at least 2 hours before anticipated incision if assigned to Arm 1, while meeting the administration requirements in Section 6 and without delaying clinically indicated surgery.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Elective surgery.
* A clinical condition that precludes safe preoperative oral medication administration or requires surgery before the planned dosing interval can be accommodated, including hemodynamic instability requiring immediate intervention, active hemorrhagic shock, inability to protect the airway, or persistent vomiting or gastrointestinal dysfunction that makes oral administration clinically inappropriate.
* Known hypersensitivity to suzetrigine or any component of the commercial tablet formulation.
* Known or clinically identified hepatic impairment of any severity, including mild, moderate, or severe impairment (Child-Pugh Class A, B, or C when applicable).
* Estimated glomerular filtration rate \<15 mL/min.
* A concurrent injury or other painful condition that, in the investigator's judgment, would substantially interfere with assessment of pain attributable to the index operation.
* Pregnancy or current breastfeeding.
* Current or anticipated use of a strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitor, or a strong or moderate CYP3A inducer, when the interaction cannot be safely avoided before and during study treatment, including consideration of persisting effects after recent discontinuation.
* Any other condition or medication interaction that, based on the clinical information available at screening, requires modification of the protocol-specified suzetrigine dose or maintenance dosing frequency or otherwise precludes safe administration of the standard regimen.
